newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West spot power flat to lower despite storm.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West spot power flat to lower despite storm.

text.p: Western U.S. spot electricity prices were flat to slightly lower Friday amid ample regional supplies and continued offers from the Bonneville Power Administration (BPA), market sources said.
"It's winter and everybody has their thermals up, but temperatures are actually pretty mild," said a Portland, Oregon, trader.
The storm, which hit the Pacific Northwest Thursday, was largely centered over Seattle and western Washington state, but weather for most of the West, including California, was mild, he added.
Sources also cited below-normal demand due to the holidays and ample hydroelectric volumes as putting downward pressure on cash market prices.
"I think we will stay in this mode until after the first (of January)," said one trader.
Firm, peak electricity at the California-Oregon border (COB) for Monday was quoted at $13.00-15.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), down slightly from Friday's prices.
Firm, off-peak COB power for Monday also was little changed at $9.00-11.00.
Monday firm, peak power at Mid-Columbia (Mid-C) was flat at $14.00-$16.00, while off-peak was quoted at $9.50-11.50.
Firm, peak Palo Verde (PV) electricity for Monday was unchanged at $14.00-18.00.
Off-peak PV for firm delivery Monday was quoted near $9.00-11.00 per MWh.
Monday firm, peak prices at Four Corners also were steady at $14.00-16.00 . Firm, off-peak Four Corners power was lower at $10.00-12.00.
